label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/sentry.mdl, models/filecabinet.mdl, models/w_egon.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, D, C, C where the asset was D, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Every view has a coherent waist-high console outline: a body box about 49 wide and 25 deep, with a raised rear panel carrying the two screens and a slanted lip at its top front. Nothing sticks out or is missing in the side, back or top views, and the outline matches the brief's words.

M2.reason: The brief gives only a height, 40 units ('waist high'). The asset is 42.5 high, 6.3% over, within 15%. Its width (49) and depth (25.2) are not asked for and are not charged.

M3.reason: The named parts are present: two green screens reading 'LEVEL 07' and 'FLOW 000' on the raised panel, and a row of eight switches (red and grey) on a dark strip. The dials are the weak point. They are three round painted dials on the top, clear only in the straight-down TOP view. In the FRONT-LEFT and FRONT-RIGHT views the top shows only faint scribbles and the dials do not read as dials at game size. They are painted, so they count, but they do not read clearly.

M4.reason: Grey-green painted metal body and panel, green phosphor screens, red and grey switches. These fit a Half-Life industrial prop and the brief's palette, and no region is an odd colour.

M5.reason: The named surface detail is present in its places: the screen lettering, the switch row, the recessed panel line and the lower slot on the front, the trim edges, and vertical rust streaks on every side. The sharpness is consistent with the rest of the mod. The dial paint's blur at size is charged under M3, not here.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. In the line-up (lineup.png) the asset sat beside the filing cabinet, the sentry and the egon, and the test passed in all four readings: judges never picked the asset as the one not made by Valve.

M7.reason: The front is correct: the screens and switch row face the viewer in FRONT, and the raised panel sits at the back. It stands upright on a flat base (BELOW view is closed and flat), with the origin at the bottom.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. The triangle count is 60, far under twice the Half-Life median of 238 for its kind. The views show a closed box with no open faces or floating parts, and the top lip looks attached in the side views.
